summary: This is a purely additive integration of a stdlib-only Python pre-processing pipeline under its own scripts/prompt_gateway/ namespace, with genuinely diligent collision-avoidance work: the staged entrypoint originally targeted the real production scripts/task-gateway.py path and was renamed/relocated, verified byte-for-byte unchanged (sha256 match) both before and after. The module never calls task-gateway.py, has no network calls, no eval/exec/subprocess, and all writable paths (data, snippets, logs, context) are namespaced under /opt/veridian/data/prompt_gateway to avoid colliding with other tools. MASTER_INDEX.yaml changes are additive registry metadata only. No .github/workflows files are touched, so the hard rule does not apply. The self-report is unusually honest about scope gaps (systemd unit correctly left uninstalled given no real streaming producer exists, classifier scoring quirk disclosed rather than hidden, 19-engine Owner spec explicitly marked not-done). A few code-quality/latent-security issues were found on direct diff review (not from the self-report) but none are reachable via the shipped CLI surface today, so they don't block a tier1 approval; they're listed for follow-up.
issues: engine/id_generator.py's IDGenerator docstring claims the counter is 'Thread-safe via file locking' but _load_counter/_save_counter do a plain read-modify-write with no fcntl/flock and no atomic temp-file-plus-rename; concurrent gateway.py invocations against the same DATA_DIR could race and either produce duplicate VD- ids or corrupt _id_counter.json. Low current risk since the module runs on-demand/CLI-only (no daemon), but the docstring is factually wrong and should be fixed or the locking actually implemented before any concurrent/daemon use.

engine/snip_engine.py's add_snippet/get_snippet/delete_snippet build file paths directly from an unsanitized `name` argument (self.snippets_dir / f'{name}.snip') with no slug validation -- a path-traversal vector (e.g. name='../../etc/cron.d/x') if a future caller ever passes external/untrusted names. Not currently reachable: the only caller in the shipped CLI is seed_defaults() with hardcoded names, so this is latent, not exploitable today, but should be sanitized (allowlist regex on name) before any code path exposes add_snippet to user-supplied input.

config.py creates real directories on disk (Path(d).mkdir(...) for base/scripts/engine/data/snippets/logs/chats/tags/context/lib) as a module-level import-time side effect, so merely `import config` -- e.g. from a future test or lint run -- writes to /opt/veridian/data/prompt_gateway regardless of intent. Not a security issue given it only touches the module's own namespace, but is an unusual/impure pattern worth cleaning up (move directory creation into init_system() or a lazy first-use call).
